tasks.spec:
You are a copywriter working for Ankit, host of the podcast "Optometrists Building Empires". Write exactly ONE file in your current working directory: ./promo_content.json. No repo writes, no git, no MCP, no network, no other files.

CRITICAL: a deterministic validator (voice_check.py) will execute against your output and REJECT it on any rule below. Two previous attempts by another writer were rejected by a human reviewer. Their exact failures are listed so you do not repeat them.

WHO IS TALKING. Ankit hosts the show. He writes blunt, short, specific, conversational. He talks in CONTRACTIONS. He is slightly impatient with fluff. He does not write LinkedIn diction. Read every line aloud in your head: if it sounds like marketing copy or a LinkedIn thought-leader post, rewrite it.

THE EPISODE (E104, guest Dr. Fred H. Cho). Real material from the actual recording — use these specifics, they are what the previous attempts lacked:
- Fred is NOT a practice owner and never has been. Eight years as an associate with a full schedule and loyal patients.
- Burnout was silent. His words: he "didn't even know what burnout even felt like until years later in hindsight". Days blurred "into months and years", a sense of monotony. No dramatic breaking point.
- He cites research on US optometrists: 54% facing some level of burnout. His line: "that's every other optometrist listening in right now". THIS IS A REAL CITED NUMBER — use it, attributed to the research Fred cites, not as your own claim.
- After burnout he did locum work only, to pay bills, and started a blog "not for money".
- The turn: he got a call to go to Manitoba. He lives in Ontario. Going to a new province "was really scary". What made it possible: a classmate already had a clinic there, so "there was a lot of trust there already". He had to learn how referrals and follow-ups worked in another province. It was a two-week locum.
- Fred's own reflection, quotable AS HIS: "sometimes the risk, the biggest risk is really not taking a risk." What used to be uncomfortable "is now just become normal to me."
- Now: licensed in Ontario, Manitoba and Newfoundland; building a team of travel optometrists. THE TEAM IS IN PROGRESS, NOT FINISHED — he is still the one on the road. Do not imply a finished team.
- Episode runtime is 37 minutes. Do NOT claim any other runtime, and do not claim a runtime at all unless it is 37.
- DO NOT claim Fred authored any book. A previous draft asserted "Author of Redesigning Work" and it is unverified. Omit it.
- DO NOT invent statistics. The ONLY number you may use is the 54% figure above, attributed to the research Fred cites.

WHAT TO WRITE — ./promo_content.json exactly this shape:
{
  "posts": [
    {"platform": "linkedin", "text": "..."},
    {"platform": "x",        "text": "..."},
    {"platform": "instagram","text": "..."}
  ],
  "email": {"subject": "...", "body": "..."}
}

THREE POSTS, THREE DIFFERENT ANGLES (a previous attempt was rejected as "one post at three lengths"):
- linkedin: the silent-burnout angle. Lead with the tension, not an announcement. Include ONE line of reader pain aimed at practice owners and associates (covering exam lanes, watching a good associate go quiet). Use the 54% figure. ONE CTA.
- x: the Manitoba-risk angle. Short and punchy. The specific detail that a classmate's clinic made the leap possible. ONE CTA.
- instagram: the "not a practice owner" angle — a different definition of an empire. ONE CTA.
Each post must be independently readable and must NOT share long sentences or phrasing with the others.

THE EMAIL is to Fred, from Ankit, telling him the episode is live and asking him to share it. Style: lowercase-ish short subject, opens "Hey Fred", 1-3 SHORT paragraphs, ONE soft CTA (not a hard ask), signs off just "Ankit". Warm and human, like Ankit typed it in two minutes. No bullet lists. No marketing phrasing.

HARD RULES THE VALIDATOR ENFORCES — violating any one fails you:
1. CONTRACTIONS in every item. Zero contractions was the single biggest rejection reason. Write "he didn't", "isn't", "you're", "that's".
2. NO em dashes anywhere. Use commas or periods.
3. NO self-answered rhetorical questions (a question followed by a 1-3 word answer, e.g. "What changed? Burnout."). Banned cadence.
4. EXACTLY ONE call-to-action signal type per post. Do not stack a listen directive AND a link AND an audience question in the same post. Pick one mechanism per post.
5. NO repeated sentences or near-duplicate phrasing across posts (no shared 8+ word sentence, and posts must not be >50% similar).
6. LINK MECHANISM must be consistent: if any post uses the placeholder {{episode_link}}, every post that links must use {{episode_link}}. Never write "Link in bio" alongside a placeholder.
7. NO unsourced statistic-shaped claims ("most doctors who burn out leave and never come back"). The 54% figure attributed to research is fine; invented generalisations are not.
8. NO sentence longer than 38 words. Keep sentences short.
9. BANNED WORDS/PHRASES, do not use any: delve, dive into, unpack, leverage, utilize, optimize, robust, seamless, streamline, foster, cultivate, bolster, landscape, ecosystem, holistic, alignment, synergy, bandwidth, revolutionary, game-changing, cutting-edge, elevate, transform, unlock, comprehensive, passionate, "I'd be happy to", "Great question", "It's important to note", "Don't miss out", "We're excited to", "just checking in", "circling back", "touching base", "hope this email finds you well", "I hope you're doing well", "wanted to reach out", "I came across", "that's on me", "my bad", "smart evolution", "no agenda here", "just wanted to say".
10. No runtime claim other than 37 minutes.

Write it, then re-read every line against rules 1-10 before you finish. Output valid JSON only in ./promo_content.json.
tasks.check: python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(open('promo_content.json')); ps=d['posts']; assert len(ps)==3, 'need 3 posts'; assert {p['platform'] for p in ps}=={'linkedin','x','instagram'}, 'platform set wrong'; assert all(len(p['text'].split())>=25 for p in ps), 'a post is too short to judge'; e=d['email']; assert e['subject'] and e['body'], 'email incomplete'; assert 'Hey Fred' in e['body'], 'email must open Hey Fred'; assert e['body'].rstrip().endswith('Ankit'), 'email must sign just Ankit'; print('SHAPE OK')" && python3 '/mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/one-true-master/checks/voice_check.py' --content promo_content.json --episode-duration-s 2218 && echo PASS
tasks.verified: three distinct-angle posts plus a guest email that pass the deterministic Ankit-voice gate on all ten rules
